summary: The nine-dot button in a suite's header and the grid of products it opens — links, each to a product's home, with the one you are in marked.
useWhen: a suite of separate products shares a header, and people move between them
the products have their own addresses: each opens at its home, in this tab or a new one

useInstead.why: sections are navigation within a product, always in view; a switcher hides them behind a button for the sake of a move people make every minute

useInstead.when: choosing a workspace or an account inside the same product
useInstead.why: that changes what the product shows, not which product it is — a menu of choices, not a set of places

useInstead.when: jumping to anything by name, products included
useInstead.why: search reaches every page by typing; the switcher is for recognising a product's mark

composition.note: Goes in Header's `end`, before the account. `apps` is the suite, in the order people look for them; `currentApp` names this product's `id`. `label` names the button, its tooltip and the panel. `footer` takes a Link to every app or to managing access.
composition.example: <Header brand={…} end={<><AppSwitcher currentApp="ops" apps={[{ id: 'ops', name: 'Ops', href: '/' }, { id: 'docs', name: 'Docs', href: 'https://docs.example' }]} /><Avatar … /></>} />

footer.note: one link under the grid, centred

requires: a `label` in the product's language when it is not English — it is the button's only name, the icon being nine dots
guarantees: the button is named by `label`, "Apps" by default, with a tooltip showing it; `aria-expanded` says whether the panel is open
the panel is a dialog named by `label`: focus moves into it and stays there, and Escape or a click outside closes it and gives focus back to the button
each product is a link, reached with Tab, so it opens in a new tab with a modifier and its address can be copied
the product you are in is `aria-current="true"` and drawn with a border as well as a tint
a product's `description` is its link's accessible description
a press on a product closes the panel, so a same-document route does not leave it open over the page it went to
in forced colours the current product's border is Highlight
notes: Not a `menu`: menu items would give up opening in a new tab and copying the address for arrow keys.
`icon` sits centred on a 40px tinted square, at its own size — a 24px icon suits. A product without one shows its initial there.

antiPatterns.dont: an AppSwitcher listing the sections of one product
antiPatterns.why: sections are moved between constantly and belong in view; a switcher is for the few moves between products

antiPatterns.dont: a Menu of products, each a MenuItem with an onAction that sets `location`
antiPatterns.why: menu items are not links: no new tab, no copied address, no status-bar URL
without it nothing says which product you are in, and the grid reads as a list of elsewheres
